key: And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite sojourning on the farther side of the hill-country of Ephraim, who took to him a concubine out of Beth-lehem in Judah.
s: The chapter in which the Levite gives his concubine up to the men of Gibeah, who abuse her all night, opens here; Metzudat David, on 19:1, reads ‘no king’ as explaining what follows: a king would have punished the sinners, sparing Israel civil war.

evidence.gloss: And there was no king in Israel: for had there been a king, what happened would not have happened, for the king would have punished the sinners, and so Israel would not have fought one another, as will be told.

Read the whole chapter 19 packet and 17:6 and 18:1 (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on Judges). Metzudat David on 19:1 says in his own words that had there been a king this would not have happened, since the king would punish the sinners and Israel would not have fought one another, as will be told: the reading is his, at this place, and the second half is kept unchanged. CORRECTED the plain sense only: the proposal said the story ‘ends with’ the concubine abused ‘to death’, but chapter 19 ends with 19:29 to 30 (the dividing of her body and the outcry), and the day’s text does not itself state her death (19:28 ‘none answered’; Rashi reads ‘for she was dead’, Metzudat David that he did not yet sense she had died; her death is stated only in 20:5, outside the day). New plain sense: ‘The chapter in which the Levite gives his concubine up to the men of Gibeah, who abuse her all night, opens here’, in the text’s own terms (19:25; Radak on 19:25 also takes the man as the Levite), one plain clause, no graphic detail, no four-word run from the verse. 43 words.
